reasons: The cited § 14.10 restricts only Customer's assignment and leaves IBM free to assign to anyone, including a competitor, so it fails the fallback's requirement of a mutual assignment right with a mutual 'consent not unreasonably withheld' standard — a material term, not a minor sub-element; deviation classification is correct.

Correctly distinguished from walk-away (M&A successor carve-out and reasonableness standard exist; no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right), so severity/classification is defensible at high.

Redline is directionally right and tracks the rule: adds the affiliate/successor (including substantially-all-assets) carve-out for Customer without consent, retains a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard for other Customer assignments, and mirrors the restriction on IBM with a no-competitor limit; it preserves the void-assignment and continuing-liability mechanics (made symmetric), so the higher changed-character ratio reflects a restructuring the rule genuinely requires rather than gratuitous rewriting.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, explains what changed and why, and offers the fallback (mutual successor assignment on written notice) as a landing zone.
